tests.exercises: Finite-volume five-moment Euler update with Roe fluxes on a one-dimensional Sod-type shock tube.
tests.why: This is in the upstream moments MOAT core acceptance set and directly exercises the fluid five-moment path. The serial initial-value problem is deterministic, so final cell states and conserved diagnostics should be compared pointwise.

tests.exercises: Ideal-MHD finite-volume update, divergence control and MHD Riemann solver on the Brio-Wu shock tube.
tests.why: This is the upstream moments MOAT MHD case and directly establishes that the approved module includes MHD. Its serial Riemann evolution is deterministic, making pointwise field and fluid-state comparison appropriate.

tests.exercises: Two-species ten-moment plasma Riemann problem coupled to Maxwell fields and the pressure-tensor update.
tests.why: This upstream MOAT case covers the ten-moment part of the approved scope, including anisotropic pressure tensors and electron-ion field coupling. The fixed serial problem is deterministic, so pointwise comparison is the natural policy.

tests.exercises: Two-dimensional five-moment electron-ion GEM magnetic reconnection with Maxwell coupling and source updates.
tests.why: This upstream MOAT problem is a substantive five-moment plasma workload and complements the fluid, MHD and ten-moment checks. The imposed GEM perturbation and serial arithmetic are deterministic; a short-window pointwise comparison preserves sensitivity to reconnection dynamics.

tests.exercises: Standalone one-dimensional Maxwell plane-wave propagation in the moments application.
tests.why: It is in the upstream moments MOAT, but it exercises the standalone Maxwell subsystem rather than fluid, MHD or five-/ten-moment plasma evolution. Maxwell coupling is already forced by the five- and ten-moment plasma checks, so this would add out-of-scope duplicate coverage.

tests.exercises: Coupled ultra-relativistic fluid and Einstein evolution on a plane-symmetric Gowdy spacetime.
tests.why: It is in the upstream moments MOAT, but general-relativistic spacetime evolution is outside the human-approved fluid, MHD and five-/ten-moment plasma scope. It should be considered only if a later GR module is approved.
